_meta.title: Chinese word list — Praise to the Twenty-One Tārās (general grade)
_meta.choices: Traditional characters · clear modern Chinese (general grade, not the chanting style) · mantra syllables in Chinese characters · flagged picks decided by Claude, with the reason written down (Tenkal, 2026-09-24).
_meta.decided_by: Claude pick — user delegated flagged picks ("go with your picks"), 2026-09-24
_meta.sources_note: (1) the classical canon version CBETA T1108B — the same text the 17th Karmapa office publishes — aligned in 0-INBOX/AI_translation/zh-references/zh-classical-T1108B.md, used for its words only; (2) the standard Buddhist term; (3) the DharmaMitra zero-shot zh draft, which suggests but never confirms. The online Mahāvyutpatti (Oslo) could not be read in this session, so "standard Buddhist term" means the well-known pair — the reviewer should check those.
_meta.baseline: the DharmaMitra zero-shot draft already uses 63 of 137 locked words (46%, check_termbase_consistency.py --lang zh). Most misses are 頂禮 for 敬禮 and mantra syllables left in Latin letters.

homage.note: Classical has 敬禮 in all 21 stanzas; DharmaMitra has 頂禮. Both are standard. 敬禮 is what Chinese practitioners already chant, and a modern reader understands it.

tara.note: Classical 救度母 / 尊聖救度母; DharmaMitra 度母 / 救度母; the Karmapa-office title uses 度母. The short name 度母 is the common modern one.

benefits.note: Standard rendering of ཕན་ཡོན; classical has no heading for it.

noble_venerable.note: རྗེ་བཙུན་ = 至尊 (standard); འཕགས་མ = 聖. Classical opening has 尊聖救度母; DharmaMitra 至尊聖救度母. Used before 度母: 至尊聖度母.

sanskrit_title.zh: Namaḥ Tārā Ekaviṃśati Stotra Guṇahita Sāka
sanskrit_title.note: The Sanskrit title line stays in IAST, as in English (zh register rule).

praise.note: Classical uses 讚 / 讚嘆 / 稱歎; DharmaMitra 讚頌. 讚頌 is the clearest modern word for བསྟོད་པ.

blessed_tara.note: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ་སྒྲོལ་མ; 世尊度母 is used in modern Tibetan-Buddhist Chinese. 薄伽梵母 would be the technical alternative (advanced grade).

perfectly.note: ཡང་དག / ཡང་དག་པར as a modifier; appears inside 圓滿具足 (1-15, 1-21). In a-1 it is part of 正等覺佛.

perfect_buddha.note: ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས = samyaksaṃbuddha = 正等覺 (standard pair). DharmaMitra wrote 正等覺如來, adding 如來 which is not in the Tibetan.

blessed_one.note: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས(མ) = 世尊. Only occurs inside 世尊度母 (a-1).

actual_praise.note: Section heading བསྟོད་པ་དངོས. DharmaMitra 正行讚頌 borrows 正行 ("main practice"), which fits a sādhana, not a section of a text. 讚頌正文 = "the praise itself".

lightning.note: Classical 電光; DharmaMitra 閃電光. 閃電 is the plain modern word.

world.note: Classical 三世界 (1-1), 七世界 (1-5). DharmaMitra mixes 三界 / 七世間界. 三界 is avoided because in Chinese it names the desire/form/formless realms (ཁམས་གསུམ), a different Tibetan word.

face.note: Classical 面 (single character, too short to lock in modern prose); DharmaMitra 面容 / 容顏. Also inside 蓮花面容 (1-8).

lotus.note: Classical 蓮華 is the same word in older spelling; 蓮花 is the modern form.

lotus_face.note: 1-8 only (her own face, likened to a lotus), as settled in the English fact-check.

blaze.note: DharmaMitra 熾燃 / 熾然 (inconsistent — locked to 熾燃); classical 熾盛. 熾燃 keeps the sense of flames.

moon.note: All sources use 月. Includes the kenning རི་དགས་རྟགས་ཅན ("deer-marked one") in 1-18, as in English.

peace.note: ཞི / ཞི་བ = 寂靜 (standard). Classical 靜 / 善靜 / 寂滅.

without_exception.note: Classical 盡無餘 / 攝無餘; DharmaMitra 無餘. Readers know 一切無餘.

trampling.note: Classical 足踏 / 踐蹋; DharmaMitra 足下踏. Single character so the verb can sit in natural phrases (踩踏, 踏於).

tuttare.note: ཏུཏྟྭ་ར. The Tārā mantra is commonly recited 嗡 達咧 都達咧 都咧 梭哈. Classical writes it three ways (怛囉 1-5, 覩怛哩 1-10, 咄怛哩 1-20); DharmaMitra left Latin. Same normalisation as the English "tuttare".

spirit.note: འབྱུང་པོ (bhūta). Classical and DharmaMitra both write the transliteration 部多, which a general reader cannot parse. 鬼神 is the ordinary Chinese word for spirits and keeps it distinct from 邪魅 (གདོན). Commentary check: Drakpa Gyaltsen, Gendun Drub and Taranatha name Gaṇapati (ཚོགས་བདག) as their chief; Taranatha: obstructers and misleaders. 鬼神 fits.

destroy.note: DharmaMitra 摧毀; classical 摧壞 / 摧滅 (same root 摧).

phat.note: ཕཊ. 呸 is the common modern Chinese form in Tibetan-Buddhist mantras; classical writes 發. Chinese characters per the user's choice.

trat.note: ཏྲད. Not part of the common mantra, so the classical form 特囉 (1-7 特囉胝發) is used.

ture.note: ཏུ་རེ. Recitation form 都咧 (嗡 達咧 都達咧 都咧 梭哈); classical 都哩.

great.note: ཆེན་མོ / ཆེན་པོ (1-8 大怖畏, 1-15 大罪). 2-3 ཆེ་བ is split out as "greater" for Chinese.

supreme.note: རབ in 1-10 (supreme joy): classical 最極喜, DharmaMitra 極喜.

power.note: དབང in 1-10 (brings māras and the world under her power). Classical 作攝伏; DharmaMitra 降伏 ("subdue by force"), which is stronger than the Tibetan. 攝伏 = bring under one's control. Commentary check: all four read དབང་དུ་མཛད as bringing under her control (Gendun Drub: the māras and the eight great worldly gods). 攝伏 fits.

joy.note: Classical 歡悅 / 喜悅 / 喜笑; DharmaMitra 喜 / 歡喜 / 極喜. The shared character 喜 is locked so compounds stay natural.

syllable_hum.note: Classical 吽字 / 吽聲; Chinese puts the syllable before 字.

ability.note: ནུས ("able to"). Chinese says this with 能 (classical 亦能鉤召 1-11, 悉能鉤召 1-5). Added 1-5 for Chinese, where the same ནུས occurs; English did not lock it there.

perfectly_endowed.note: ཡང་དག་ལྡན (1-15, 1-21). DharmaMitra 圓滿具足; classical 皆具足.

mantra.note: སྔགས. Classical 呪 is a variant of 咒; DharmaMitra alternates 咒 / 真言 — locked to 咒 (根本咒 1-22, 十字咒 / 明咒 1-16).

goddess.note: ལྷ་མོ (2-1). 天女 is the usual Chinese for lha mo / devī (cf. 吉祥天女). Kept distinct from 世尊 (བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ), as in English. Commentary check 2026-09-24: Gendun Drub (ལྷ་མོ་སྒྲོལ་མ) and Taranatha (= བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ) identify ལྷ་མོ with Tārā herself. Reviewer: if 天女 reads as a lesser celestial being, use 聖尊 or 女尊.

vetala.note: རོ་ལངས ("risen corpse"): classical 起屍 (1-6). DharmaMitra has 起屍 in 1-21 but 羅剎 (rākṣasa, a different being) in 1-6 — Phase 2 must correct 1-6. Commentary check: Taranatha glosses རོ་ལངས as a class of beings (ལྷའི་སྲིན་པོའི་རིགས་དགུ), which may be why DharmaMitra wrote 羅剎; the word itself is "risen corpse", so 起屍 stays.

empowerment.note: དབང in 2-3 (the Victors confer empowerment). Classical benefits section 灌頂.

demon.note: གདོན (afflicting spirits). DharmaMitra 魔 / 鬼 — but 魔 is needed for བདུད (Māra) in 1-8 and 1-10. Classical 執魅 (1-21) points to 魅. 邪魅 = harmful spirits. Commentary check: Taranatha — the eighteen གདོན (e.g. ནམ་གུའི་གདོན); Drakpa Gyaltsen — all that obstructs. 邪魅 (harmful spirits) fits.

yaksha.note: གནོད་སྦྱིན. Classical 藥叉 is the older spelling of the same word.

might.note: མཐུ (1-21): classical 善靜威力; DharmaMitra 威德力.

greater.note: Chinese-only split from "great": ཆེ་བ in 2-3 is comparative ("greater than this"), so 大 does not fit. DharmaMitra 更勝者. Commentary check: Gendun Drub — the common great siddhis; Taranatha — many greater qualities. 更殊勝 fits.

om.note: Chinese-only entry: English left mantra syllables unlocked. 嗡 is the common modern form; classical 唵.

svaha.note: Chinese-only entry. Recitation form 梭哈; classical 莎訶.

hara.note: Chinese-only entry. Not part of the common mantra; classical 1-20 誦二喝囉.

tara_syllable.note: Chinese-only entry. 1-18 "reciting TĀRA twice": the recitation form 達咧 (as in 嗡 達咧 都達咧), same normalisation as tuttare. Classical 誦二怛囉.
